title: Text structure Practice 1
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused text structure questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Cool Roof Pilot

Several apartment roofs absorbed intense afternoon heat. Owners coated three roofs with a reflective surface and left three unchanged. Indoor temperatures were then compared during similar weather.

TEXT B - Mangrove Roots

Mangrove roots slow moving water and trap sediment. As sediment collects, shorelines can become more stable, and sheltered areas may provide habitat for young fish.

TEXT C - Two Reminder Systems

Text reminders are inexpensive and reach phones quickly. Voice calls can take more staff time but may work better for clients who rarely read texts. A clinic compares both before choosing a mixed system.

TEXT D - Archive Scan

First, staff remove staples from fragile documents. Next, each page is scanned. After files are checked, the originals return to protective folders and digital copies are added to the catalog.

questions.prompt: Which text structure best describes this passage?
questions.explanation: The passage presents a heat problem, tests a reflective coating as a response, and compares coated with unchanged roofs.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: problem / solution supported by a comparison
cause / effect only
options.whyWrong: Heat and temperature effects appear, but the passage is organized around a tested response to a problem.

options.text: sequence / process
options.whyWrong: The events occur in order, but the main organization is not a set of instructions or steps for the reader.

options.text: classification / description
options.whyWrong: The passage does not group roofs into categories simply to describe them.

questions.prompt: How does that structure help develop the passage?
questions.explanation: The organization lets readers see both the proposed solution and how its performance was evaluated.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It mainly lists roof features so readers can classify different building types.
options.whyWrong: The comparison is used to evaluate a response, not to create categories of buildings.

options.text: It focuses on the chronological order of installing the coating rather than whether it worked.
options.whyWrong: Installation order is secondary to the problem/solution evaluation.

options.text: It shows the heat problem, the tested response, and evidence comparing the response with unchanged roofs.
It presents two equally supported solutions and asks readers to choose between them.
options.whyWrong: The unchanged roofs are a comparison group, not a competing solution.

questions.prompt: Which text structure best describes this passage?
questions.explanation: Roots slowing water and trapping sediment lead to later shoreline stability and habitat effects.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: description only
options.whyWrong: The passage does more than describe roots; it traces consequences of what roots do.

options.text: problem / solution
options.whyWrong: No central problem is introduced and solved.

options.text: cause / effect
sequence / process
options.whyWrong: The passage explains consequences, not a procedure readers should follow.

questions.prompt: How does that structure help develop the passage?
questions.explanation: Cause-and-effect structure helps readers connect the actions of roots with the results that follow.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It groups mangrove roots into types based on where they grow.
options.whyWrong: No categories of roots are presented.

options.text: It compares mangroves with another shoreline plant using the same criteria.
options.whyWrong: Only mangrove roots and their effects are described.

options.text: It gives step-by-step instructions for planting mangroves.
options.whyWrong: The text explains natural effects rather than planting steps.

options.text: It traces how the roots' physical effects can lead to later shoreline and habitat outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which text structure best describes this passage?
questions.explanation: The passage weighs strengths and limitations of text reminders and voice calls before noting a mixed system.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: cause / effect
options.whyWrong: The main relationship is between two methods, not one event causing another.

options.text: compare / contrast leading to a combined choice
sequence / process
options.whyWrong: The passage does not teach a series of steps.

options.text: problem / solution with only one proposed response
options.whyWrong: Two methods are compared before a combined approach is chosen.

questions.prompt: How does that structure help develop the passage?
questions.explanation: The comparison supports the later decision because readers can see why neither method is ideal for every client.

options.text: Comparing the strengths and limits of both methods gives a basis for choosing a mixed system.
It shows that voice calls caused text reminders to become less effective.
options.whyWrong: The passage compares methods; it does not say one caused the other to fail.

options.text: It organizes the methods by the order in which the clinic first adopted them.
options.whyWrong: Adoption chronology is not the organizing principle.

options.text: It describes two methods without connecting the comparison to a decision.
options.whyWrong: The comparison explicitly leads toward a mixed system.

questions.prompt: Which text structure best describes this passage?
questions.explanation: Signal words such as First, Next, and After organize the archive-scanning procedure step by step.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: cause / effect
options.whyWrong: The passage is organized by order of actions rather than consequences.

options.text: compare / contrast
options.whyWrong: No two scanning methods are weighed against each other.

options.text: problem / solution
options.whyWrong: The main purpose is to explain a procedure, not solve a stated problem.

options.text: sequence / process

questions.prompt: How does that structure help develop the passage?
questions.explanation: Sequence structure makes the workflow clear because each action depends on its place in the process.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It shows why removing staples causes digital copies to be added to the catalog.
options.whyWrong: The actions occur in sequence, but the text does not frame each step as a causal chain.

options.text: The step-by-step order helps readers follow the document-scanning procedure from preparation to storage.
It compares the advantages of paper archives with digital archives.
options.whyWrong: The passage explains one workflow rather than evaluating two archive systems.

options.text: It classifies documents according to how fragile they are.
